lesson.title: Pass in Two
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: They are coming in and covering the obvious passing lane. Your contact is low behind the baseline.

tf1A.name: Choose from the volley they actually play.
tf1A.sit: The low volley lands shorter through the middle. They are still near the centre of the net.
tf1A.q: Choose from the volley they actually play.
opts: Use the shorter contact to pass into space
Lift with depth to regain time

lines.A: You use the shorter ball to pass left of their coverage. Stay ready.
lines.B: A sound way to reset. The shorter volley also offered a passing opportunity.

tf1A.take: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1A.payoff: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1A.principle: Make the first volley difficult. Read it before you pass.
tf1A.why: A dipping ball can force the net player to volley upward and create a more playable next ball. The sideline is not forbidden, but forcing it from low contact gives little margin. Neither reply is guaranteed: watch the actual volley before choosing again.

tf1B.name: Choose from the volley they actually play.
tf1B.sit: Their firmer volley is deep to your backhand. The passing opportunity has become harder.
tf1B.q: Choose from the volley they actually play.
opts: Use the shorter contact to pass into space
Lift with depth to regain time

lines.A: This pass lands, but the deeper contact gives you less room to force it.
lines.B: You adapt to the deeper volley and buy time.

tf1B.take: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1B.payoff: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1B.principle: Make the first volley difficult. Read it before you pass.
tf1B.why: A dipping ball can force the net player to volley upward and create a more playable next ball. The sideline is not forbidden, but forcing it from low contact gives little margin. Neither reply is guaranteed: watch the actual volley before choosing again.

tf1.name: Can you make their first volley difficult?
tf1.sit: They are coming in and covering the obvious passing lane. Your contact is low behind the baseline.
tf1.q: Can you make their first volley difficult?
opts: Dip the ball toward their feet

lines.A: They have to volley below the net. Read where that volley actually goes.
lines.B: They reach your pass above the net and send the volley deeper. You must adjust.

tf1.take: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1.payoff: Build the pass in two balls. Read the volley before choosing again.
tf1.principle: Make the first volley difficult. Read it before you pass.
tf1.why: A dipping ball can force the net player to volley upward and create a more playable next ball. The sideline is not forbidden, but forcing it from low contact gives little margin. Neither reply is guaranteed: watch the actual volley before choosing again.

summaries.10: The first choice fitted. The next ball needed a fresh decision.
summaries.11: Both choices fitted the contact and court you had. Keep reading as the point changes.
summaries.01: You adapted on the second ball. Compare what the first choice cost.
summaries.00: Compare the first choice, then read the next contact again. A landing alone does not prove a sound decision.

comparison.intro: Hold the incoming situation fixed. Change the first shot and watch the reply.

lesson.completionIntro: Your first choice changed the next ball. Read each contact afresh.
lesson.redoLabel: Try another route through this point

pro.label: Chang · The first pass is a question
pro.moment: Rafter was asked whether his net play made him almost impossible to pass at the 1997 US Open. He immediately rejected the idea. Chang, he explained, often made him play “a tough and low volley” instead of trying for a winner on the first pass.
pro.read: Your next point: make the first volley difficult. Then read the ball that comes back before choosing your second pass.
pro.src: Pat Rafter · US Open press conference · 6 September 1997

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Start with a partner approaching. Play a low first pass, then call the actual volley’s depth before selecting the second shot. Change the volley direction each time.
